The provided script `fchat-horizon.sh` is a simple launcher script that executes the Electron 43 runtime with an ASAR archive located at `/usr/share/fchat-horizon/app.asar`, passing along all command-line arguments (`"$@"`). The use of `exec` ensures the current shell is replaced by the Electron process, which is standard practice for application launchers.

The script does not perform any network operations, file modifications, or system changes. It does not contain obfuscated code, dangerous commands (like `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or `base64`), or any logic that could exfiltrate data or execute unauthorized code. The path `/usr/share/fchat-horizon/app.asar` is a standard location for packaged Electron applications in Linux distributions, and ASAR archives are a legitimate way Electron bundles application code.

While the script relies on the integrity of the ASAR file and the Electron binary, these are part of the broader package installation process and not indicative of malicious behavior in the script itself. There is no evidence of supply-chain compromise or injected malicious logic in this file.
</details>
